note: Persistent-brief B2B outreach building blocks: the 8 brief sections with the evidence each is built from, copy constraint rows (first-touch, follow-up, DM, subject), the 5-part cold-call script spine, pipeline health flags, sequence-metric triage thresholds, and the first-week ramp. This bank is authored, not measured — the metric thresholds are the pattern's rules of thumb, and agents must not present anything here as 'proven'. A fuller playbook with the full prompt set lives in the shared skills shelf as the outreach-brief-gtm skill; the core pattern: build a canonical brief once from real deal evidence, load it into every session, and have every copywriting and analysis step read it instead of re-asking. Hard rules that travel with every row: the brief holds honest weaknesses, pricing, and deal history and is private context never quoted in outbound copy; sends and automations that enroll prospects stay human-approved. Slots are UPPERCASE so an unfilled template trips the placeholder check in src/lib/services/deliverables/acceptance-contracts.ts.

briefSections.holds: what you actually sell, the honest case for buying, where positioning is generic, what a sceptic challenges first
briefSections.evidence: the real competitive record, not the marketing copy

briefSections.holds: actual value propositions ranked by frequency in won deals, split rational vs emotional, mapped to persona
briefSections.evidence: won-deal notes, referral language, renewal reasons

briefSections.holds: one-sentence offer, specific outcome promise, believability proof, risk reversal, low-friction CTA
briefSections.evidence: what buyers needed to believe before saying yes

briefSections.holds: firmographic, technographic, and behavioural criteria, disqualifiers, and the one 60-second qualifying question
briefSections.evidence: won, lost, and churned deal patterns

briefSections.holds: title range, top pressures, the buyer's own problem language, what they distrust in cold outreach, tone to use
briefSections.evidence: discovery-call notes in the buyer's words

briefSections.holds: per competitor: their self-positioning, where each side is genuinely stronger, the landmine discovery question, the response when preferred
briefSections.evidence: deals actually lost to and won against each

briefSections.holds: TAM/SAM/SOM with methodology, sources, key assumptions, and the assumption most likely wrong
briefSections.evidence: the ICP definition plus reachable-motion capacity

briefSections.holds: the 5 pains most frequent in won deals, each in the buyer's words, what they tried before, and the make-them-feel-understood question
briefSections.evidence: won-deal calls, ranked by urgency x frequency x ability to relieve

copyConstraints.rules: opener references a specific signal; body under 75 words, one pain, one outcome, no feature list; one low-friction CTA that is not book-a-call; subject under 7 words
copyConstraints.gate: if the email could have been sent to any company, rewrite it

copyConstraints.rules: each touch a completely different angle; stands alone as if earlier touches were never sent; never checking-in or circling-back; last touch is the break-up; all under 75 words
copyConstraints.gate: no touch may reference that a previous email was sent

copyConstraints.rules: under 200 characters, references something specific, no pitch
copyConstraints.gate: two variants drafted, one marked to send

copyConstraints.rules: under 150 characters, adds value or opens conversation, no pitch before a conversation exists
copyConstraints.gate: second DM after five silent days takes a new angle, not a follow-up

coldCallSpine.name: opening
coldCallSpine.rule: one sentence, a specific reason for calling this person now

coldCallSpine.name: permission
coldCallSpine.rule: ask for thirty seconds before anything else

coldCallSpine.name: pain question
coldCallSpine.rule: one question that opens the conversation without pitching

coldCallSpine.name: value bridge
coldCallSpine.rule: connect their pain to the outcome in two sentences

coldCallSpine.name: ask
coldCallSpine.rule: a specific next step, never can-I-send-you-some-info; prep the three likeliest objections with exact responses

pipelineFlags.flag: no next step with a date attached
close date passed with no update
root-cause each flagged deal: ICP fit, wrong stakeholder, no pain, price, timing, or competitor

metricTriage.onMiss: below 3% triggers a rewrite of the worst touch

firstWeek.do: install, run onboarding, review the generated brief and correct anything wrong
first-touch for the top ten accounts, follow-ups for touches two through five, load into the sequencer
LinkedIn DMs for the same ten accounts, cold-call script for the primary persona
reply-rate audit on the week's sends, pipeline review on replies, fold the week's lessons back into the brief
weekly strategist review: three highest-leverage changes, sequenced, with success metrics
